answer: The karst test I would run is Proof of unique conference talk video record: talks recorded at four conferences over five years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. Each account presents its proof once, the network verifies it in seconds, and a farm that wants ten accounts must pass ten independent checks — the ocean is that the work cannot be shared or replayed. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the sable of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
